definition: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining, a model trained to align images and text descriptions in a shared embedding space using contrastive learning.
details: CLIP learns to associate images with their natural-language descriptions from large web-scraped datasets, enabling zero-shot image classification and forming a key building block for many text-to-image and multimodal systems.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. Think of it this way: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining, a model trained to align images and text descriptions in a shared embedding space using contrastive learning. And here is the clever part: CLIP learns to associate images with their natural-language descriptions from large web-scraped datasets, enabling zero-shot image classification and forming a key building block for many text-to-image and multimodal systems. The shape of the machine is half the idea. And that shape of the machine — CLIP — is what makes everything else possible.

citation.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
